hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.lead: Answers to the most important questions about our intensive care services.

questions.q: Is intensive care at home really possible?
questions.a: Yes — in many cases, comprehensive intensive care can be provided right in your own home. The prerequisite is a doctor's prescription for home nursing care.
We care for patients throughout Hesse — from Volkmarsen and Kassel to Frankfurt and beyond.

questions.q: Who bears the cost of intensive care?
questions.a: In most cases, the costs are fully covered by health and care insurance. We take care of all communication with the funding bodies.

questions.q: Is the care level relevant for 24h care?
questions.a: 24-hour intensive care is primarily funded through §37 SGB V and is not directly tied to the care level. A higher care level may unlock additional benefits.

questions.q: How long does it take until care begins?
questions.a: From the initial consultation to the start of care, it typically takes 4 to 6 weeks.

questions.q: What qualifications does your nursing staff have?
questions.a: All medically prescribed measures are carried out exclusively by certified nursing professionals who are regularly trained by specialist physicians.

questions.q: What does the residential care concept include?
questions.a: In our assisted living projects, we offer clients private rooms, a garden, a library, and 24h care with 5.5 staff members per client.
Via the quick application form on our website, by phone, or by email to pflege@ksk-farmos.de.

questions.q: How does the transition from hospital to home work?
questions.a: We handle the entire transition management. Our team coordinates a seamless handover in close consultation with hospital staff and organizes all necessary medical equipment.

questions.q: Do we have to buy medical equipment ourselves?
questions.a: No. All medical devices such as ventilators and monitors are provided by the health insurance. We work closely with specialized medical technology companies.

questions.q: Are nursing staff present at night as well?
questions.a: Yes. With 24-hour intensive care, a certified nurse is always on-site — including at night — to ensure continuous and safe monitoring.
